title: Surge diffuser and graceful rejoin orchestrator (proportional falloff + tenant soft-reinstate)
author: Anika Patel
release_notes: Adds a proportional surge diffuser for regional load spikes and a graceful rejoin orchestrator that staggers tenant reinstatement to avoid post-failover thundering. Backwards-compatible config flags and telemetry added.
description:
Context: Recent incidents showed rapid post-failover rejoin (region -> global) causing concentrated bursts that trip local SLO enforcers and oscillate circuits. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: 1) a proportional 'surge diffuser' which converts sudden regional capacity shortfalls into controlled, priority-weighted shedding over a configurable window; 2) a 'graceful rejoin orchestrator' that sequences tenant reinstatement (soft-reinstate) with adjustable ramp profiles to avoid thundering and allow KV-cache warmup.

Motivation: We want to reduce oscillation and repeat circuit flips after regional failover events, ensure higher-priority tenants regain capacity first, and give runtime subsystems (KV cache, batching warm pools) time to stabilize before full traffic is restored.

Summary of changes:
- New runtime controller: runtime/surge/diffuser.go — implements proportional falloff based on tenant weight, request histograms, and SLO headroom. Diffuser emits per-tenant allowance tokens over a sliding window rather than immediate binary shed decisions.
- Graceful rejoin orchestrator: orchestration/rejoin/orchestrator.go — coordinates tenant reinstatement across the cluster, supports linear and exponential ramp profiles, and integrates with the existing canary/rollout APIs.
- Config: config/defaults.yaml — new stanza 'surge_diffuser' and 'rejoin_orchestrator' with sensible defaults and feature gates.
- Telemetry: metrics/metering.go — adds diffuser_allowance_gauge, rejoin_phase_gauge, and rejoin_lag_histogram; also hooks for tracing rejoin cohorts.
- Tests: unit tests for diffuser logic and end-to-end integration in tests/e2e/rejoin_cohort_test.go.
- Docs: docs/operational/surge-diffuser.md — operational runbook and tuning guidance.

Checklist:\n- [x] Design review (SRE + Runtime)\n- [x] Unit tests (diffuser logic corner cases)\n- [x] E2E test simulating regional failover with 3 cohorts\n- [x] Telemetry validated in staging\n- [x] Rollout plan and feature flag gated

Implementation details and rationale: The diffuser uses a proportional algorithm so tenants with higher SLO priority receive a larger share of the limited allowance. The allowance is computed from: local capacity deficit, recent tail-latency breach rate, and tenant weight. This avoids strict priority cutoff which previously starved mid-tier tenants. The rejoin orchestrator groups tenants into cohorts (size configurable) and issues soft-reinstate tokens per cohort. Soft-reinstate means the router accepts the tenant's traffic but annotates requests with a cohort id and a short-lived 'rejoin token' so that downstream caches can warm with predictable traffic shaping. The orchestrator includes safety hooks: if tail latency or error rate worsens during a cohort ramp, the orchestrator pauses and backoffs using exponential cool-down.

Compatibility and ops: All behavior is behind two feature gates: feature.surge_diffuser and feature.rejoin_orchestrator. Default state in this PR is 'off' for dedicated clusters and 'on' for staging. Operators can tune cohort size, ramp window, and proportional weights in config. Metrics added are exposed to Prometheus and we added a Grafana dashboard (docs link) for observability.

Commits:\n- 1a2b3c4: runtime: initial surge diffuser core algorithm and interfaces\n- 2b3c4d5: orchestration: rejoin orchestrator and cohort model\n- 3c4d5e6: telemetry: expose allowance and phase gauges; add tracing hooks\n- 4d5e6f7: tests: unit and e2e for diffuser + rejoin interactions\n- 5e6f7g8: docs: operational runbook, rollout notes, dashboard links\n- 6f7g8h9: hotfix: adjust throttle threshold to prevent under-shedding on bursty embeddings

Files changed (high-level):\n- runtime/surge/diffuser.go\n- orchestration/rejoin/orchestrator.go\n- config/defaults.yaml\n- metrics/metering.go\n- tests/e2e/rejoin_cohort_test.go\n- docs/operational/surge-diffuser.md\n- dashboards/rejoin-diffuser.json (grafana template)

reviews: Marcus Liu (SRE): Left a couple of nits on the tracing tags. Asked for an additional e2e with cache-warmup verification. Marked as APPROVED after tests were added.
Ravi Menon (Runtime): Suggested proportional weighting instead of percentile thresholds — updated implementation accordingly. Verified concurrency safety for allowance counter.
Claire Novak (Eng Lead): Requested operational runbook and rollout gates; approved after runbook added and staging telemetry ok.
review_thread:
Marcus: The tracing span needs tenant.id and cohort.id (so we can correlate warmup).
Anika: Added cohort.id to the span and added a short-lived rejoin token annotation.

Ravi: computeAllowance may be expensive in hot paths; can we cache recent values per node?
Anika: Added an atomic snapshot per-100ms window to avoid recalculation on every request.

Claire: Rollout plan?
Anika: Feature flag gated; staged rollout over 48 hours with automated rollback on >2% tail-latency regression.
incident_correlation: Related to incident INC-2024-09-14 where post-failover rejoin caused repeated circuit trips; this PR is the recommended mitigation from postmortem ENG-4512.
rollout_plan: 1) Enable feature in staging for 24h and validate rejoin metrics; 2) Canary on 5% of traffic in prod with cohort_size=4; 3) Full rollout over 48h if no regressions; auto-disable on >1.5% increase in 99th latency for any cohort.
operational_notes: Operators can tune 'default_cohort_size', 'window_seconds', and per-tenant weights. If unexpected backlog occurs, set feature.surge_diffuser=false to revert to legacy shedders. Dashboard 'Rejoin & Diffuser' added with cohort lag, allowance utilisation, and rejoin pause events.
post_merge_actions: 1) Monitor staging and prod dashboards for 72h. 2) Run canary eviction drills to validate rejoin safety. 3) Follow-up PR to add runtime CLI knobs to dynamically adjust cohort size.
merge_summary: Merged via squash. Small hotfix commit adjusted throttle threshold after initial perf smoke — included in the squash. All CI green at merge time.
notes_for_backport: Backport to release/2024-11 required only if running legacy SLO-enforcement; backport excludes dashboards and docs. Backport branch: release/2024-11-surge-diffuser-backport.
acknowledgements: Thanks to SRE triage (Marcus), Runtime review (Ravi), and UX for runbook edits (Claire).
